data.case_title: Suspicious "Last Warning Before Seizure" Letter Demanding Broadcasting Fee Payment (Likely Scam)
data.explanation: This letter claims to be from a "Zahlungszentrale" collecting broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) arrears of 254.35 EUR and threatens account/wage seizure if you don't pay within the deadline shown. Several details strongly suggest this is a scam rather than a genuine notice from the official Beitragsservice: the payment account is in Lithuania, not Germany; the letter tells you not to contact the address you already know for the Beitragsservice; contact is only possible by e-mail; and there is extreme, unusual time pressure. Do not transfer any money or click links. Instead, verify directly with the official Beitragsservice (using contact details you already have or find independently, not those in this letter) whether any real arrears exist, and consider reporting this letter to the police (Anzeige wegen Betrugsversuchs). Keep the letter as evidence and do not reply from the e-mail address it provides.

data.summary: A letter styled "LETZTE MAHNUNG VOR PFÄNDUNG" claims Sam Rivera owes 254.35 EUR in overdue broadcasting fees (Rundfunkbeitrag) for 2025, plus late fees and a processing charge, and demands payment within 48 hours of receipt to a foreign (Lithuanian) bank account, threatening immediate account/wage seizure otherwise. Multiple features of the letter are typical of a payment-collection scam impersonating the official Beitragsservice.
data.title: Suspicious "Last Warning Before Seizure" Letter Demanding Broadcasting Fee Payment (Likely Scam)
warnings: The payment IBAN (LT08 3999 0000 0543 9871) is Lithuanian; the German Beitragsservice does not collect fees to foreign private accounts — this is a strong scam indicator.
The payee name includes 'Beitragsinkasso UAB' (a Lithuanian company form), inconsistent with the German public broadcaster fee agency.
The letter explicitly instructs you not to contact the known/official Beitragsservice address and offers only an e-mail contact, which is a common tactic to prevent victims from verifying the claim.
The Beitrags-Nr. (623 918 044) shown here does not match the previously known Beitragsnummer (512 345 678) for this household's Beitragsservice account.

An extremely short 48-hour payment deadline with threats of immediate enforcement and no formal legal basis or Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung is atypical for genuine German administrative dunning procedures and is a pressure tactic often used in scams.
The sender's e-mail domain ('rundfunk-beitragservice.example') is not the official rundfunkbeitrag.de domain.
